51.title: Rooted Where You Are: A Prayer from Psalm 1 | Evening Meditations
51.desc: A reading of Psalm 1, the picture of a tree planted by streams of water. Tonight you can stop asking why you were put in a dry place and start noticing that the roots can still reach water. The prayer asks God to grow something good in you right where you are. Scripture: Psalm 1:1-3.

52.title: My Refuge and My Strength: A Breath Prayer (Psalm 46:1) | Evening Meditations
52.desc: A short breath prayer from the first line of Psalm 46. Breathe in "You are my refuge," breathe out "You are my strength," and keep going on your own in the quiet. God is not a help that shows up late. He is already in the middle of whatever you are facing tonight. Scripture: Psalm 46:1.

53.title: His Love Endures: A Gratitude Prayer (Psalm 136:1-3) | Evening Meditations
53.desc: A gratitude prayer built on the line that repeats twenty-six times in Psalm 136: his love endures forever. You will name something that lasted through today, someone who stayed, and the love that does not end. It is a good prayer for anyone who has learned how rare lasting things can be. Scripture: Psalm 136:1-3.

54.title: Why Do You Stand Far Off? A Lament Prayer (Psalm 10:1) | Evening Meditations
54.desc: A lament for the nights when God feels far away. Psalm 10 asks the question out loud, and tonight you can ask it too. You will tell God where he seems distant, what you need him to see, and ask him to come close. If you cannot say "You see me" yet, "I want to believe you do" is an honest prayer. Scripture: Psalm 10:1.

55.title: When You Are on Your Bed, Be Silent: A Prayer of Stillness (Psalm 4:4) | Evening Meditations
55.desc: A stillness prayer for bedtime. Psalm 4 says that when you are on your bed, you should search your heart and be silent, because the quiet is when you finally hear yourself. After a short reading we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "be silent" and "I'm here." Scripture: Psalm 4:4.

56.title: Answer Me When I'm in Trouble: A Blessing for the Week (Psalm 20:1-4) | Evening Meditations
56.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Psalm 20, a prayer that God would answer you in distress, protect you, and send help. You will finish by thinking of someone who may need help this week and asking God to send it, maybe through you. Scripture: Psalm 20:1-4.

57.title: Examine My Heart and Mind: An Evening Examen (Psalm 26:2) | Evening Meditations
57.desc: An examen built on a brave prayer: Lord, examine my heart and my mind. You will look at what you actually thought about today, what it says about what you care about and fear, and what to set down. It ends with one true and good thing to keep your mind on tomorrow. Scripture: Psalm 26:2.

58.title: Mindful of You: A Prayer from Psalm 8 | Evening Meditations
58.desc: A reading of Psalm 8 under a wide night sky. The God who set every star in place is mindful of you, and he has crowned you with glory and honor, no matter what anyone else has called you. The prayer is a slow reminder of who you are tonight. Scripture: Psalm 8:3-5.

59.title: Good News of Great Joy: A Christmas Eve Breath Prayer (Luke 2:10-11) | Evening Meditations
59.desc: A Christmas Eve breath prayer from the words the angel spoke to shepherds on a night shift. Breathe in "Do not be afraid," breathe out "Good news of great joy," and keep going on your own in the quiet. If this is a hard night to be apart from the people you love, this prayer is for you too. Scripture: Luke 2:10-11.

60.title: An Indescribable Gift: A Christmas Day Gratitude Prayer (2 Corinthians 9:15) | Evening Meditations
60.desc: A gratitude prayer for Christmas Day. Paul ran out of words and called Jesus an indescribable gift. You will say thank you for that gift, for something you were given this year, and for something you could give. The prayer also remembers everyone who is missing someone today. Scripture: 2 Corinthians 9:15.

61.title: Every Sigh Is Heard: A Lament Prayer (Psalm 38:9, 15) | Evening Meditations
61.desc: A lament for people who are worn out from carrying it all alone. Psalm 38 says your sighing is not hidden from God, so tonight you let it out. You will name what you long for, what you are tired of carrying, and end with the writer's words: Lord, I wait for you. Scripture: Psalm 38:9 and Psalm 38:15.

62.title: Not Shaken: A Quiet Prayer of Stillness (Psalm 16:8-9) | Evening Meditations
62.desc: A stillness prayer from Psalm 16, written by someone who kept his eyes on one thing so that nothing else could shake him. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "eyes on You" and "not shaken." Scripture: Psalm 16:8-9.

63.title: Strength and Peace: A Blessing for the Week (Psalm 29:11) | Evening Meditations
63.desc: A short blessing for the week ahead from Psalm 29. God gives strength to his people and blesses them with peace, two things you cannot make for yourself. You will finish by thinking of one person who needs strength or peace this week. Scripture: Psalm 29:11.

64.title: Turn My Steps: An Evening Examen (Psalm 119:59-60) | Evening Meditations
64.desc: An examen for looking at the road you walked today. You will ask which way you were headed, where you took a good step, and where you went the wrong way, without shame. Then you pick one small step to take tomorrow. Scripture: Psalm 119:59-60.

65.title: You Are My Portion: A Prayer from Psalm 16 | Evening Meditations
65.desc: A reading of Psalm 16:5-6 about the portion God gives. The writer talks about boundary lines and calls them pleasant, because his real portion is God himself. Tonight you can choose where to look for your portion, whatever walls are around you. Scripture: Psalm 16:5-6.

66.title: A New Thing: A New Year's Eve Breath Prayer (Isaiah 43:19) | Evening Meditations
66.desc: A breath prayer for the last night of the year. God says he is doing a new thing, making a way in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland, even before we can see it. Breathe in "You are doing a new thing," breathe out "Help me see it," and let the year go. Scripture: Isaiah 43:19.

67.title: Crown the Year: A New Year's Day Gratitude Prayer (Psalm 65:11) | Evening Meditations
67.desc: A gratitude prayer for the first day of the year. Psalm 65 says God crowns the year with his bounty, so tonight you look back and say thank you. You will name something good from last year, something that got you through, and something you are hoping for this year. Scripture: Psalm 65:11.

68.title: Wake Up, Lord: A Lament Prayer (Psalm 44:23-26) | Evening Meditations
68.desc: A lament for when God seems to be asleep. Psalm 44 says "Awake, Lord!" out loud, and tonight you can too. You will tell God where it feels like he is not moving, what you are going through, ask him to rise up and help, and hold on to his unfailing love. Scripture: Psalm 44:23-26.

69.title: One Thing: A Quiet Prayer of Stillness (Psalm 27:4) | Evening Meditations
69.desc: A stillness prayer built on Psalm 27:4, where the writer asks for one thing only: to be near God and gaze on his beauty. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "one thing" and "your presence." Scripture: Psalm 27:4.

70.title: The Lord Remembers Us: A Blessing for the Week (Psalm 115:12-15) | Evening Meditations
70.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Psalm 115. The Lord remembers us and will bless us, small and great alike, and that includes the people you love. You will finish by thinking of someone near or far and asking God to bless them this week. Scripture: Psalm 115:12-15.

71.title: A Guard Over My Mouth: An Evening Examen (Psalm 141:3-4) | Evening Meditations
71.desc: An examen about your words. You will look at what you said today that built someone up, what tore someone down, and what was underneath it. Then you choose one kind thing to say to one person tomorrow. Scripture: Psalm 141:3-4.

72.title: The Lord Is My Rock: A Prayer from Psalm 18 | Evening Meditations
72.desc: A reading of Psalm 18:1-6, where the writer names God his rock, fortress, shield, and stronghold, then cries out from the tangle and is heard. A slow prayer for a night when you need something solid to stand on. Scripture: Psalm 18:1-6.

73.title: Perfect Peace: A Breath Prayer from Isaiah 26:3 | Evening Meditations
73.desc: A breath prayer from Isaiah 26:3. Breathe in "Perfect peace," breathe out "I trust You," and keep going on your own in the quiet. When your mind wanders, you just come back to the words. Scripture: Isaiah 26:3.

74.title: With All My Heart: A Gratitude Prayer from Psalm 9 | Evening Meditations
74.desc: A gratitude prayer from Psalm 9:1-2. You will name one wonderful thing God did today, one thing you are glad about, and one person you could tell about his goodness. Scripture: Psalm 9:1-2.

75.title: Oh, That I Had Wings: A Lament from Psalm 55 | Evening Meditations
75.desc: A lament from Psalm 55:1-8 for a night when you want to run away from your thoughts, your fears, or this place. The writer says it out loud to God, and so can you. There is no pressure to fix anything. Scripture: Psalm 55:1-8.

76.title: Our Help and Our Shield: A Stillness Prayer from Psalm 33:20 | Evening Meditations
76.desc: A stillness prayer built on Psalm 33:20. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "help" and "shield." Scripture: Psalm 33:20.

77.title: Bless You from Zion: A Blessing for the Week (Psalm 134) | Evening Meditations
77.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Psalm 134, a song for people who serve through the night. You will lift your hands in thanks and receive a blessing for the days to come. Scripture: Psalm 134.

78.title: Lean Not on Your Own Understanding: An Evening Examen (Proverbs 3:5-6) | Evening Meditations
78.desc: An examen from Proverbs 3:5-6. You will look at where you trusted God today, where you relied only on yourself, and what you can hand over. Then you choose one step for tomorrow. Scripture: Proverbs 3:5-6.

79.title: The Heavens Declare: A Prayer from Psalm 19 | Evening Meditations
79.desc: A reading of Psalm 19:1-4 under a wide night sky. Night after night the heavens speak without words, and their voice reaches everyone, including you. Scripture: Psalm 19:1-4.

80.title: When I Am Afraid: A Breath Prayer from Psalm 56:3 | Evening Meditations
80.desc: A breath prayer from Psalm 56:3. Breathe in "When I am afraid," breathe out "I trust You," and keep going on your own in the quiet. For a night when fear is loud. Scripture: Psalm 56:3.

81.title: This Very Day: A Gratitude Prayer from Psalm 118:24 | Evening Meditations
81.desc: A gratitude prayer from Psalm 118:24. You will name something small and good from today, something hard you got through, and someone who helped you. Scripture: Psalm 118:24.

82.title: List My Tears: A Lament from Psalm 56:8 | Evening Meditations
82.desc: A lament from Psalm 56:8, which says God keeps a record of our tears. You will tell him what hurts and know that nothing you have cried over has gone unseen. Scripture: Psalm 56:8.

83.title: Through the Watches of the Night: A Stillness Prayer from Psalm 63 | Evening Meditations
83.desc: A stillness prayer built on Psalm 63:6-8, a prayer for the night hours. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two phrases: "I cling to you" and "your right hand upholds me." Scripture: Psalm 63:6-8.

84.title: The God Who Has Been My Shepherd: A Blessing for the Week (Genesis 48:15-16) | Evening Meditations
84.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Genesis 48:15-16, the blessing Jacob spoke over his grandsons. You will receive it for yourself and ask God to shepherd a young person you love. Scripture: Genesis 48:15-16.

85.title: A Gentle Answer: An Evening Examen (Proverbs 15:1) | Evening Meditations
85.desc: An examen from Proverbs 15:1. You will look at where you stayed gentle today, where you got sharp, and who you might make peace with. Then you picture a gentle answer for tomorrow. Scripture: Proverbs 15:1.

86.title: Let the King of Glory Come In: A Prayer from Psalm 24 | Evening Meditations
86.desc: A reading of Psalm 24:7-10, where the gates are told to open for the King of glory. A slow prayer for opening one closed door in your own heart. Scripture: Psalm 24:7-10.

87.title: Fearfully and Wonderfully Made: A Breath Prayer from Psalm 139:14 | Evening Meditations
87.desc: A breath prayer from Psalm 139:14. Breathe in "Wonderfully made," breathe out "Thank You," and keep going on your own in the quiet. A reminder of who you are tonight. Scripture: Psalm 139:14.

88.title: Let Us Exalt His Name Together: A Gratitude Prayer from Psalm 34 | Evening Meditations
88.desc: A gratitude prayer from Psalm 34:1-3. You will name something you can praise God for, lift up someone who is hurting, and give thanks for someone you can praise him with. Scripture: Psalm 34:1-3.

89.title: Has God Forgotten Me? A Lament from Psalm 77 | Evening Meditations
89.desc: A lament from Psalm 77:1-9 for a night when God feels far away and the questions are heavy. The writer asks them out loud, and so can you. Scripture: Psalm 77:1-9.

90.title: Better Is One Day in Your Courts: A Stillness Prayer from Psalm 84:10 | Evening Meditations
90.desc: A stillness prayer built on Psalm 84:10. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "better" and "near." Scripture: Psalm 84:10.

91.title: He Will Never Leave You: A Blessing for the Week (Deuteronomy 31:6) | Evening Meditations
91.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Deuteronomy 31:6. Be strong and courageous, for the Lord your God goes with you and will never leave you. Scripture: Deuteronomy 31:6.

92.title: Commit to the Lord Whatever You Do: An Evening Examen (Proverbs 16:3) | Evening Meditations
92.desc: An examen from Proverbs 16:3 about your work and your plans. You will look at what you did today, where you forgot God in it, and what plan you are holding too tightly. Scripture: Proverbs 16:3.

93.title: According to Your Love, Remember Me: A Prayer from Psalm 25 | Evening Meditations
93.desc: A reading of Psalm 25:1-7, a prayer for guidance and mercy. Teach me your paths, and according to your love, remember me. Scripture: Psalm 25:1-7.

94.title: Taste and See: A Breath Prayer from Psalm 34:8 | Evening Meditations
94.desc: A breath prayer from Psalm 34:8. Breathe in "Taste and see," breathe out "The Lord is good," and keep going on your own in the quiet. Scripture: Psalm 34:8.

95.title: What Shall I Return to the Lord? A Gratitude Prayer from Psalm 116 | Evening Meditations
95.desc: A gratitude prayer from Psalm 116:12-13. You will name something good you received, remember a time God rescued you, and choose how to respond. Scripture: Psalm 116:12-13.

96.title: Restore Us, Make Your Face Shine: A Lament from Psalm 80 | Evening Meditations
96.desc: A lament from Psalm 80:1-7, a cry to the Shepherd to restore what is broken and let his face shine again. You will name what needs restoring in you and in the people you love. Scripture: Psalm 80:1-7.

97.title: Return to Your Rest, My Soul: A Stillness Prayer from Psalm 116:7 | Evening Meditations
97.desc: A stillness prayer built on Psalm 116:7. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "rest" and "good." Scripture: Psalm 116:7.

98.title: Underneath Are the Everlasting Arms: A Blessing for the Week (Deuteronomy 33:27) | Evening Meditations
98.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Deuteronomy 33:27. The eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms. Scripture: Deuteronomy 33:27.

99.title: The Lord’s Purpose Prevails: An Evening Examen (Proverbs 19:21) | Evening Meditations
99.desc: An examen from Proverbs 19:21. You will look at the plans you made today, what did not go your way, and where God's purpose may be showing up. Scripture: Proverbs 19:21.

100.title: The Lord Is My Light: A Prayer from Psalm 27 | Evening Meditations
100.desc: Night 100 of Evening Meditations. A reading of Psalm 27:1-5. The Lord is my light and my salvation, so whom shall I fear? A slow prayer for a night when you need a place to be hidden and safe. Scripture: Psalm 27:1-5.

101.title: Show Me Your Ways: A Breath Prayer from Psalm 25:4-5 | Evening Meditations
101.desc: A breath prayer from Psalm 25:4-5. Breathe in "Show me your ways," breathe out "My hope is in You," and keep going on your own in the quiet. Scripture: Psalm 25:4-5.

102.title: The Lord Has Done Great Things: A Gratitude Prayer from Psalm 126:3 | Evening Meditations
102.desc: A gratitude prayer from Psalm 126:3. You will remember a great thing God has done in your life, a good thing he has done for someone you love, and a small joy from today. Scripture: Psalm 126:3.

103.title: I Spread Out My Hands to You: A Lament from Psalm 88 | Evening Meditations
103.desc: A lament from Psalm 88:1-9, the darkest psalm in the Bible, for a night when everything feels dark. You do not have to wrap it up. You only have to reach out your hands. Scripture: Psalm 88:1-9.

104.title: Our Eyes Look to the Lord: A Stillness Prayer from Psalm 123:2 | Evening Meditations
104.desc: A stillness prayer built on Psalm 123:2. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "look" and "mercy." Scripture: Psalm 123:2.

105.title: Under His Wings: A Blessing for the Week (Ruth 2:12) | Evening Meditations
105.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Ruth 2:12. Under the wings of the God of Israel, you are safe. You will ask God to bless someone who showed you kindness. Scripture: Ruth 2:12.

106.title: The Lord Weighs the Heart: An Evening Examen (Proverbs 21:2) | Evening Meditations
106.desc: An examen from Proverbs 21:2 about being honest with yourself. You will look at what you are proud of, where you made excuses, and what God sees underneath. Scripture: Proverbs 21:2.

107.title: The Lord Is My Strength and My Shield: A Prayer from Psalm 28 | Evening Meditations
107.desc: A reading of Psalm 28:6-7. The Lord has heard your cry for mercy, and he is your strength and your shield. A prayer for finding a song after the crying. Scripture: Psalm 28:6-7.

108.title: Your Unfailing Love: A Breath Prayer from Psalm 143:8 | Evening Meditations
108.desc: A breath prayer from Psalm 143:8. Breathe in "Your unfailing love," breathe out "I trust You," and keep going on your own in the quiet. Scripture: Psalm 143:8.

109.title: Sing to the Lord with Grateful Praise: A Gratitude Prayer from Psalm 147:7 | Evening Meditations
109.desc: A gratitude prayer from Psalm 147:7. You will give thanks for a song you love, a person who brings you joy, and a moment of peace from today. Scripture: Psalm 147:7.

110.title: Rise Up, Judge of the Earth: A Lament from Psalm 94 | Evening Meditations
110.desc: A lament from Psalm 94:1-7, a cry for justice when wrong seems to be winning. You will bring what has been done to you, or to someone you love, to the Judge of the earth. Scripture: Psalm 94:1-7.

111.title: In Quietness and Trust: A Stillness Prayer from Isaiah 30:15 | Evening Meditations
111.desc: A stillness prayer built on Isaiah 30:15. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "quietness" and "trust." Scripture: Isaiah 30:15.

112.title: Oh, That You Would Bless Me: A Blessing for the Week (1 Chronicles 4:10) | Evening Meditations
112.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from 1 Chronicles 4:10, the prayer of Jabez. It is okay to ask God for a blessing, and to ask that his hand be with you. Scripture: 1 Chronicles 4:10.

113.title: They Rise Again: An Evening Examen (Proverbs 24:16) | Evening Meditations
113.desc: An examen from Proverbs 24:16. You will look at where you fell today, where you got back up, and how you will rise again tomorrow. Scripture: Proverbs 24:16.

114.title: Rejoicing Comes in the Morning: A Prayer from Psalm 30 | Evening Meditations
114.desc: A reading of Psalm 30:1-5. Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning. A slow prayer for a heavy night and the hope that it will not last. Scripture: Psalm 30:1-5.

115.title: Remain in Me: A Breath Prayer from John 15:5 | Evening Meditations
115.desc: A breath prayer from John 15:5. Breathe in "I remain in You," breathe out "You remain in me," and keep going on your own in the quiet. Scripture: John 15:5.

116.title: Giving Thanks for Everything: A Gratitude Prayer from Ephesians 5:20 | Evening Meditations
116.desc: A gratitude prayer from Ephesians 5:20. You will name something easy to thank God for, something you have taken for granted, and something hard you can only hand to him for now. Scripture: Ephesians 5:20.

117.title: Save Me from Lying Lips: A Lament from Psalm 120 | Evening Meditations
117.desc: A lament from Psalm 120:1-2 for anyone who has been lied about or lied to. You will tell God who has hurt you with their words, and leave your defense in his hands. Scripture: Psalm 120:1-2.

118.title: Quietness and Confidence: A Stillness Prayer from Isaiah 32:17 | Evening Meditations
118.desc: A stillness prayer built on Isaiah 32:17. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "quietness" and "confidence." Scripture: Isaiah 32:17.

119.title: His Eyes Range Throughout the Earth: A Blessing for the Week (2 Chronicles 16:9) | Evening Meditations
119.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from 2 Chronicles 16:9. The eyes of the Lord are looking for hearts turned to him, to strengthen them. Scripture: 2 Chronicles 16:9.

120.title: Reflecting the Heart: An Evening Examen (Proverbs 27:19) | Evening Meditations
120.desc: An examen from Proverbs 27:19. You will look at what your day shows about your heart, and choose one small step toward a heart that loves what is good. Scripture: Proverbs 27:19.

121.title: Into Your Hands I Commit My Spirit: A Prayer from Psalm 31 | Evening Meditations
121.desc: A reading of Psalm 31:1-5, the psalm Jesus prayed from the cross. Into your hands I commit my spirit. A prayer for the end of the day. Scripture: Psalm 31:1-5.

122.title: Strength to Get Through: A Breath Prayer from Philippians 4:13 | Evening Meditations
122.desc: A breath prayer from Philippians 4:13, written by Paul from prison. Breathe in "Give me strength," breathe out "I can get through this," and keep going on your own in the quiet. Scripture: Philippians 4:13.

123.title: His Love Endures Forever: A Gratitude Prayer from 1 Chronicles 16:34 | Evening Meditations
123.desc: A gratitude prayer from 1 Chronicles 16:34. You will give thanks that God is good, for a love in your life that has lasted, and for one good thing from today. Scripture: 1 Chronicles 16:34.

124.title: Have Mercy on Us: A Lament from Psalm 123 | Evening Meditations
124.desc: A lament from Psalm 123:1-4 for anyone who has been treated with contempt. You will lift your eyes to the God who sees you and hear that you are worth more than what they said. Scripture: Psalm 123:1-4.

125.title: Renew Their Strength: A Stillness Prayer from Isaiah 40:28-31 | Evening Meditations
125.desc: A stillness prayer built on Isaiah 40:28-31. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "weary" and "renew." Scripture: Isaiah 40:28-31.

126.title: My Unfailing Love Will Not Be Shaken: A Blessing for the Week (Isaiah 54:10) | Evening Meditations
126.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Isaiah 54:10. Though the mountains be shaken, his unfailing love for you will not be. Scripture: Isaiah 54:10.

127.title: Confess and Find Mercy: An Evening Examen (Proverbs 28:13) | Evening Meditations
127.desc: An examen from Proverbs 28:13. You will bring into the light what you have been hiding and receive the mercy that is already yours. Scripture: Proverbs 28:13.

128.title: You Forgave the Guilt of My Sin: A Prayer from Psalm 32 | Evening Meditations
128.desc: A reading of Psalm 32:1-5. Silence made the writer sick, and honest confession set him free. A slow prayer for bringing what you've been carrying into the light and being forgiven. Scripture: Psalm 32:1-5.

129.title: I Will Not Be Shaken: A Breath Prayer from Psalm 16:8 | Evening Meditations
129.desc: A breath prayer from Psalm 16:8. Breathe in "You are at my right hand," breathe out "I will not be shaken," and keep going on your own in the quiet. Scripture: Psalm 16:8.

130.title: A Kingdom That Cannot Be Shaken: A Gratitude Prayer from Hebrews 12:28 | Evening Meditations
130.desc: A gratitude prayer from Hebrews 12:28. You will give thanks for what cannot be shaken, for the shaking you survived, and for something that fills you with awe. Scripture: Hebrews 12:28.

131.title: How Can We Sing? A Lament from Psalm 137 | Evening Meditations
131.desc: A lament from Psalm 137:1-4 for anyone far from home who has lost their song. You do not have to sing tonight. You only have to tell God what you miss. Scripture: Psalm 137:1-4.

132.title: Come, All You Who Are Thirsty: A Stillness Prayer from Isaiah 55:1-3 | Evening Meditations
132.desc: A stillness prayer built on Isaiah 55:1-3. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "come" and "listen." Scripture: Isaiah 55:1-3.

133.title: Like a Well-Watered Garden: A Blessing for the Week (Isaiah 58:11) | Evening Meditations
133.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Isaiah 58:11. Even in a sun-scorched land, the Lord will guide you, satisfy your needs, and make you like a well-watered garden. Scripture: Isaiah 58:11.

134.title: Give Careful Thought to Your Ways: An Evening Examen (Haggai 1:5-7) | Evening Meditations
134.desc: An examen from Haggai 1:5-7. You will look at where you spent your effort today, whether it satisfied you, and whether it is going where you most want it to go. Scripture: Haggai 1:5-7.

135.title: Your Unfailing Love Be with Us: A Prayer from Psalm 33 | Evening Meditations
135.desc: A reading of Psalm 33:18-22. The eyes of the Lord are on those who hope in his unfailing love. A prayer for waiting, trusting, and being kept. Scripture: Psalm 33:18-22.

136.title: The Strength of My Heart: A Breath Prayer from Psalm 73:26 | Evening Meditations
136.desc: A breath prayer from Psalm 73:26. Breathe in "You are the strength of my heart," breathe out "You are my portion," and keep going on your own in the quiet. Scripture: Psalm 73:26.

137.title: Praise and Thanks and Honor: A Gratitude Prayer from Revelation 7:12 | Evening Meditations
137.desc: A gratitude prayer from Revelation 7:12. You will thank God for a time he gave you strength, a moment of wisdom, and someone who showed you honor. Scripture: Revelation 7:12.

138.title: I Will Not Keep Silent: A Lament from Job 7:11 | Evening Meditations
138.desc: A lament from Job 7:11 for a night when you need to say the true thing out loud. God lets Job complain, and he lets you too. Scripture: Job 7:11.

139.title: He Lives with the Lowly: A Stillness Prayer from Isaiah 57:15 | Evening Meditations
139.desc: A stillness prayer built on Isaiah 57:15. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "with" and "revive." Scripture: Isaiah 57:15.

140.title: A Tree Planted by the Water: A Blessing for the Week (Jeremiah 17:7-8) | Evening Meditations
140.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Jeremiah 17:7-8. Blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord, like a tree planted by water, green even in a year of drought. Scripture: Jeremiah 17:7-8.

141.title: Act Justly, Love Mercy, Walk Humbly: An Evening Examen (Micah 6:8) | Evening Meditations
141.desc: An examen from Micah 6:8. You will look at whether you acted justly, loved mercy, and walked humbly with God today, and choose one act for tomorrow. Scripture: Micah 6:8.

142.title: In Your Light We See Light: A Prayer from Psalm 36 | Evening Meditations
142.desc: A reading of Psalm 36:5-9. God's love reaches to the heavens, and his wings are a refuge. A slow prayer for a night when you need light. Scripture: Psalm 36:5-9.

143.title: Renew My Strength: A Breath Prayer from Isaiah 40:31 | Evening Meditations
143.desc: A breath prayer from Isaiah 40:31. Breathe in "I hope in You," breathe out "Renew my strength," and keep going on your own in the quiet. Scripture: Isaiah 40:31.

144.title: I Thank My God Every Time I Remember You: A Gratitude Prayer from Philippians 1:3 | Evening Meditations
